clue.text: Label new kit etc.

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over afresh into a different order

explanation.surface: A tag on a fresh set of kit and other things.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket is a tag or label attached to goods.

clue.text: Spare the top man, being thoughtful

parts.note: spare means lean, thin
a king is the top man of a realm

explanation.surface: Show mercy to the chief, being considerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinking means reflecting or pondering, being contemplative.

clue.text: To bend about at one is good for one's health

indicators.note: about tells us the bend is placed around the other letters here

parts.note: to curve is to bend
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Stretching around at once is beneficial.
explanation.definitionFit: Curative means healing, able to remedy illness.

clue.text: Cheese found in part of dilapidated Amsterdam

indicators.note: found in tells us the letters sit within part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cheese discovered in a run-down district of the Dutch city.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a round Dutch cheese with a red wax coat.

clue.text: Make a song about heat in crowds

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece sits round the other here

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
heat as warmth, warm

explanation.surface: Singing about the hot weather while surrounded by people.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarming describes things moving together in great numbers, like a throng.

clue.text: Making a pot-won't like to proceed carefully

indicators.note: making means building something out of these letters in a new order

explanation.surface: Fashioning crockery won't make you walk delicately.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking on tiptoe means moving quietly and cautiously, avoiding notice.

clue.text: Drops the right article in

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Lets the correct item fall into place.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain is falling drops of water.

clue.text: Very cold? It depends!

parts.note: depends is read literally as hangs down, as something frozen hangs from a gutter

explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is frozen water that hangs from eaves.

clue.text: Fish swallowing the cockle

indicators.note: swallowing means the fish takes the other word inside it

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish eating the shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cockle' looks like the shellfish, but as a verb it means to pucker or wrinkle, as cloth does when it gathers.
explanation.definitionFit: To cockle is to pucker or wrinkle, as fabric gathered into folds.

clue.text: An encroachment on the fashionable way

parts.note: in means fashionable
a road is a way

explanation.surface: Trespassing on the trendy route.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is an advance into someone else's territory, a gradual intrusion.

clue.text: It's plain stupid for a mountaineer

indicators.note: stupid tells us the letters are muddled up foolishly into a new order

explanation.surface: It is obviously foolish to be a climber.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpinist is a climber of high peaks, originally the Alps.

clue.text: People trained in a down-to-earth way

definitions.text: People trained in a down-to-earth way

parts.words: People trained in a down-to-earth way
parts.note: down-to-earth is read literally as descending from the sky to the ground

explanation.definitionFit: Parachutists are trained to drop from aircraft and float to the ground.

clue.text: Children may get a line on this bird

definitions.text: Children may get a line on this bird

parts.words: Children may get a line on this bird
parts.note: the bird is not a living one but a toy flown on a string by children, with a bird's name

explanation.surface: Youngsters can attach a string to this flier.
explanation.definitionFit: A kite is both a bird of prey and a paper toy flown on a string.

clue.text: The domestic fowl is obviously covered

definitions.meaning: a castrated cockerel raised for the table
wearing a hat for all to see

explanation.surface: The farmyard bird is plainly wearing something on its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a fattened castrated rooster; split in two, the letters describe a person with headgear on.

clue.text: Light rod-about a pound

indicators.note: about places the rod around the pound sign in this light

parts.note: a cue is a rod used in billiards
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: A lightweight stick weighing roughly one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue throws light on a problem, a hint helping understanding.

clue.text: To expose about fifty would be sound

indicators.note: about tells us one word wraps around the Roman numeral here

parts.note: to bare is to expose
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Revealing roughly fifty things would be sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: A blare is a loud harsh noise, like a trumpet blast.

clue.text: A revolting individual

parts.note: revolting read not as disgusting but as rising in revolt against authority

explanation.definitionFit: A rebel is one who rises up against authority, an insurgent.

clue.text: Engagements in the main

parts.note: engagements are fights rather than betrothals, and the main is the open sea

explanation.definitionFit: Naval battles are combats fought at sea, the main being an old word for the ocean.

clue.text: Back up the big family and there's strong criticism

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to back is to aid or support
a tribe is a large family group

explanation.surface: Support the large clan and you get a fierce attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a tirade.

clue.text: Most austere holy men keep a bird

indicators.note: keep means the holy men hold the bird between them

parts.note: ST is an abbreviation for saint, so two saints give two such abbreviations
an erne is a sea eagle

explanation.surface: The strictest monks keep a pet bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Sternest means harshest or severest in manner.

clue.text: The poor staid ill-used surgeon

indicators.note: ill-used suggests these letters are badly treated and knocked out of order

explanation.surface: An impoverished, stuffy doctor who has been mistreated.
explanation.definitionFit: An orthopaedist is a surgeon specialising in bones and joints.

clue.text: Timid guy setting a crowd at odds

indicators.note: at odds suggests these letters are in disagreement and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A fearful man who puts a gathering against itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward is a person lacking courage, a fearful one.

clue.text: Call for a comedian!

explanation.surface: Ring for a funny man!
explanation.definitionFit: A scream is a loud cry; an extremely funny person is also called a scream.

clue.text: Not now applied to cigarette ends

parts.note: on means applied to, as a plaster is put on

indicators.note: ends picks the first and last letters of the word cigarette

explanation.surface: No longer stuck on the tips of a smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some time in the past rather than at present.

clue.text: One point over 500 will be tolerated

parts.note: S, south, is one point of the compass
too means over or excessively
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A single mark beyond 500 will be put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: Stood means put up with or endured, as in 'could not stand it'.

clue.text: Agitate for porridge

explanation.surface: Mix up the breakfast oats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porridge' looks like the thing being stirred, but it is British slang for time in prison, as is STIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to agitate or mix; both stir and porridge are British slang for a prison sentence.

clue.text: Money that's taken in after some business

indicators.note: after puts this word behind the business in this clue

parts.note: Co is short for company, a business

explanation.surface: Cash that's received following a company deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Coin is metal currency, cash.

clue.text: Inferior ground

explanation.surface: Poor-quality land.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means low or ignoble; it is also a foundation, the grounding of something.

clue.text: The pub appears a dreadful hole with wear and tear

indicators.note: dreadful indicates the letters are put in a terrible state, rearranged

parts.note: use means wear and tear, as in signs of use

explanation.surface: The bar looks like an awful dump, worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears' and 'with' are link words; 'dreadful' rearranges the hole to give LEHO after the A.
explanation.definitionFit: An alehouse is a tavern, an inn where beer is served.

clue.text: Parasites follow a well-qualified person for spite

indicators.note: follow places the parasites after the qualified person in this clue

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a holder of a degree
lice are parasites

explanation.surface: Bugs trail after a graduate out of ill will.
explanation.definitionFit: Malice is the desire to harm, ill will or spite.

clue.text: Reduce by taking food with little in it

indicators.note: with little in it means the small word goes inside the food

parts.note: a dish is a serving of food
mini means little

explanation.surface: Cutting down by eating meals with tiny portions.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to make or become smaller, to lessen.

clue.text: Rue crack about exercise

indicators.note: about tells us the crack surrounds the exercise here

parts.note: a rent is a tear or crack
PE is physical education, exercise

explanation.surface: Regret a split around a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: To rue is to regret, to feel sorry for one's misdeeds.
